title: Record ESC-26: an inherited request marker opens pull requests nobody asked for
body:
One row appended to `docs/escapes.md`. No code.

**What happened.** `docs/design-r8-s3-r26-units-correction` carries a `docs/DESIGN.md` correction. `AGENTS.md` is explicit that such a branch is written by an agent and opened by the owner: *"You may write them, commit them, and push the branch… You may not open the pull request. Push the branch, say its name in your report, and stop."*

The branch was pushed with **no** `.pr-request.json` added. The App opened **#182** for it anyway, titled *"Retire the FetchFailure re-export alias (OD-12, half 2 of 2)"* — #181's title and #181's body, describing a change that is not in the diff.

**Why.** `open-pr.yml` decides by existence alone:

```
if [ ! -f .pr-request.json ]; then ... nothing to do
```

under the comment *"No request file means this push is not asking for a pull request."* That holds only if the marker is absent by default. It is not — it sits at the repository root, is committed on the requesting branch, and **merges into the base with it**. Every branch cut from the base inherits the last merged request.

**Why the row matters more than this one incident.** `owner-authored.sh` caught #182 and named the reason correctly. But it fired only because the branch touched `docs/DESIGN.md`. Any other branch — a scratch push, a branch parked for review, a work-in-progress left deliberately unopened — inherits the same stale marker and opens a pull request that passes every check while its title and body describe a different change. Nothing compares the marker against the diff or against the branch, and the review gate is handed that stale body as the author's own account of the work.

The candidates are in the row. The cheapest is to make the marker name its own branch and refuse on a mismatch, which turns a silent mislabelling into the loud failure the same workflow's header already says it prefers.

`.github/workflows/open-pr.yml` is a CODEOWNERS-owned gate path, so the fix is the owner's, and it belongs upstream in the template where the workflow is owned.

Ran locally against this diff: `plan-resolve.sh`, `escapes-append-only.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
